objectives: Recognize the canonical zoonoses (rabies, Lyme, brucellosis, leptospirosis, toxoplasmosis, influenza).
Apply the Schwabe → Manhattan Principles → Quadripartite One Health framework.
Reason about emerging spillover (SARS, H5N1, COVID-19) + the Daszak/Karesh surveillance architecture.

slides.title: Zoonoses: the shared-pathogen interface
slides.body:
**Zoonoses** = diseases transmissible between vertebrate animals + humans. Approximately **60% of all known human infectious diseases** + **~75% of emerging infectious diseases** are zoonotic (Jones et al. 2008 *Nature*; Taylor et al. 2001). Veterinarians sit at the sentinel position — most spillovers reach a vet's attention before they reach human medicine.

**Modes of transmission**:
- **Direct contact** (saliva, bite, scratch, blood, urine): rabies, brucellosis, bartonellosis (cat-scratch disease), pasteurellosis, leptospirosis.
- **Vector-borne**: Lyme (Ixodes ticks), West Nile (Culex mosquitoes), plague (fleas), Rickettsial fevers (ticks, fleas, mites), Chagas (kissing bugs), trypanosomiasis (tsetse).
- **Foodborne**: salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, *E. coli* O157:H7, Listeria, toxoplasmosis (undercooked meat), brucellosis (raw milk + cheese), trichinellosis.
- **Waterborne**: leptospirosis, cryptosporidiosis, giardiasis.
- **Aerosol/respiratory**: psittacosis (Chlamydia psittaci, birds), Q fever (Coxiella burnetii, ruminant placenta + parturition), tuberculosis (M. bovis, M. tuberculosis complex), hantavirus (rodent excreta), influenza.
- **Environmental**: anthrax (Bacillus anthracis spores in soil), tularemia (rabbits + rodents).

**Canonical zoonoses every clinician must know**:

**Rabies** — *Lyssavirus* (Rhabdoviridae); 100% fatal once clinical (with rare exceptions — Milwaukee protocol survivors). ~59,000 human deaths globally per year; ~40% are children; ~95% from dog bites in countries without canine rabies control. **Reservoir varies by region**: dogs in Asia + Africa + Latin America; raccoons + skunks + foxes + bats in North America. The **canine rabies-vaccination program** has eliminated dog-mediated human rabies from most of Europe + the Americas + remains the cornerstone of WHO/WOAH/FAO's **'Zero by 30'** goal (zero human dog-mediated rabies deaths by 2030). **Bat rabies** is the dominant US human source (~70% of US human cases, often after unrecognized bat exposure in bedroom). **Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)**: wash wound + HRIG (human rabies immune globulin) into wound + IM rabies vaccine series on days 0/3/7/14 (immunocompetent) — 100% effective if started before symptoms. **Veterinarians**: pre-exposure vaccination + 6-month titer recommended; the AVMA + CDC Compendium of Animal Rabies Prevention is the operational reference.

**Lyme disease** — *Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato* (B. burgdorferi in US, B. afzelii + B. garinii in Europe); transmitted by *Ixodes scapularis* (deer tick) + *I. pacificus* (US west coast) + *I. ricinus* (Europe). Reservoirs: white-footed mouse + small mammals; deer maintain tick populations. **Dogs**: ~5-10% of seropositive dogs show clinical Lyme — lameness (Lyme arthritis), Lyme nephritis (protein-losing, often fatal, esp. Labradors + Goldens; ACVIM consensus statement 2018). **Diagnosis**: SNAP 4Dx + QC6 quantitative + UPC for protein-losing nephritis. **Treatment**: doxycycline 10 mg/kg q12h × 28 d. **Prevention**: aggressive tick prevention (isoxazoline class — fluralaner, sarolaner, lotilaner) + Lyme vaccine in endemic regions. **Humans**: erythema migrans, arthritis, carditis, neuroborreliosis; doxycycline standard.

**Brucellosis** — *Brucella abortus* (cattle, bison), *B. melitensis* (sheep + goats; most pathogenic human strain), *B. suis* (swine + feral hogs), *B. canis* (dogs). **Undulant fever** in humans — recurrent fever, sweats, malaise, hepatosplenomegaly, arthritis, endocarditis, abortion. Transmission via unpasteurized dairy, contact with parturient + aborted material, occupational (veterinarians, farmers, abattoir workers, hunters). Largely controlled in US/EU livestock through test-and-slaughter eradication programs (US Bangs program, RB51 calfhood vaccine). Reservoir in US: feral hogs (B. suis), Yellowstone bison + elk (B. abortus), military dog colonies (B. canis). Treatment: doxycycline + rifampin or streptomycin × 6 wk. Lab safety: BSL-3 pathogen, frequent cause of laboratory-acquired infection.

**Leptospirosis** — spirochete *Leptospira* spp; many serovars. Reservoirs: rodents + dogs + livestock + wildlife. Transmitted via urine-contaminated water + mud. **Dogs**: classic icteric (canicola + icterohaemorrhagiae) syndrome or pulmonary hemorrhage; AKI + hepatic injury. **Cattle**: abortion + milk drop + infertility (hardjo serovar). **Humans**: Weil's disease — fever, hepatic + renal failure, pulmonary hemorrhage. Bivalent (4-serovar) canine vaccine; doxycycline treatment + prophylaxis.

slides.title: Foodborne, parasitic, + emerging zoonoses
slides.body:
**Toxoplasmosis** — *Toxoplasma gondii*; obligate intracellular apicomplexan. **Cats** are the definitive host (only species in which the parasite completes its life cycle, shedding oocysts in feces for ~2 wk after first infection). Other warm-blooded animals + humans are intermediate hosts harboring tissue cysts. **Transmission to humans**: (1) consumption of undercooked meat with tissue cysts (the largest source — pork, lamb, venison, wild game), (2) ingestion of sporulated oocysts from cat feces (~24 h after shedding) in contaminated soil/water/produce, (3) **congenital** — primary infection in pregnant women → fetal infection → chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications, stillbirth. **Immunocompromised** (AIDS, transplant) → reactivation toxoplasmic encephalitis. **Cat ownership** is a modest risk factor (mostly via soil + litter exposure); pregnant women should NOT change litter daily (litter must sit ~24 h for oocysts to sporulate before becoming infectious) + should wear gloves gardening + cook meat to safe internal temperature. The disease is **far more associated with undercooked meat than with cats** — a public-health message often inverted in popular media.

**Avian influenza A — H5N1 + the 2024 dairy-cattle event**:
- **Influenza A** has segmented RNA genome → **reassortment** in coinfected hosts produces novel strains. The 1918 H1N1 'Spanish flu', 1957 H2N2, 1968 H3N2, 2009 H1N1 pandemics emerged from animal reservoirs.
- **H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI)**: lineage emerged in 1996 (Guangdong goose) + caused major poultry + wild-bird outbreaks 1997+. Goose/Guangdong-derived clades have spread globally via wild waterfowl migration. **2021-2024**: clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1 caused unprecedented North + South American outbreaks affecting poultry + wild birds + mammals (foxes, seals, sea lions, marine mammals, dairy cattle).
- **2024 US dairy-cattle outbreak**: HPAI H5N1 (B3.13 genotype) detected in dairy cattle (first ever sustained mammalian dairy outbreak), spread via milking equipment + cow movement; ~67 confirmed human cases (mostly mild — conjunctivitis + URI) as of late 2024. USDA Federal Order requires interstate testing; FDA confirms pasteurization inactivates virus; CDC monitors workers. This is precisely the One Health/Schwabe + Karesh + Daszak surveillance scenario — wildlife (waterfowl) → poultry → cattle → human spillover.
- **Human pandemic potential**: H5N1 case-fatality rate in detected human cases historically ~50%, though selection bias for severe cases. Adaptation to mammalian transmission is the watched signal.

**SARS-CoV-1 + MERS-CoV + SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) — coronavirus spillover**:
- **SARS-CoV-1** (2002-03): horseshoe-bat origin via masked palm civets in Guangdong wet markets → ~8000 human cases, ~10% case-fatality; contained by traditional public-health measures.
- **MERS-CoV** (2012+): bat-origin via dromedary camels (intermediate + ongoing reservoir) → endemic in Arabian Peninsula; ~2600 cases, ~35% CFR; sporadic nosocomial outbreaks (Korea 2015).
- **SARS-CoV-2** (2019+): bat-origin (closest known: RaTG13 + pangolin betacoronaviruses); **first major detection at the Huanan seafood market**, Wuhan; pandemic caused >700M confirmed cases + ~7M reported deaths (likely several-fold higher actual). Origin debate: zoonotic spillover (most likely per scientific consensus + WHO 2021 report) vs. research-related (under investigation). Either way, the One Health surveillance principle applies — wildlife trade + research interface + emerging disease.
- **Veterinary role**: SARS-CoV-2 has infected dogs, cats, ferrets, mink (massive Danish + Dutch farm outbreaks 2020 → cull of ~17M mink), white-tailed deer (extensive US wildlife reservoir), zoo big cats, gorillas. Veterinarians + wildlife biologists are essential to the surveillance + reverse-zoonosis problem.

**Ebola, Marburg, Nipah, Hendra, MERS, Lassa, henipaviruses** — bat-reservoir viruses with periodic spillover, often through intermediate amplifying hosts (Nipah → pigs/Malaysia 1998; Hendra → horses/Australia 1994; SARS → civets; MERS → camels; Ebola → ?). The bat-reservoir theme is consistent + central to modern emerging-disease ecology.

**Rickettsial + tick-borne**: anaplasmosis, ehrlichiosis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, babesiosis, southern tick-associated rash illness, alpha-gal syndrome (Lone Star tick → mammalian-meat allergy), Heartland virus, Bourbon virus, Powassan virus — the tick-borne disease catalog is expanding fast under climate-driven range expansion.

**Anthrax** — *Bacillus anthracis*; soil-spore reservoir; herbivore infection (sheep + cattle); cutaneous + inhalational + GI human forms; biothreat agent (Amerithrax 2001).

**Plague** — *Yersinia pestis*; flea-rodent cycle; endemic in US southwest prairie-dog colonies + reservoirs in central Asia + Africa. Bubonic + septicemic + pneumonic forms.

slides.title: One Health architecture: Schwabe → Manhattan Principles → Quadripartite + the future of pandemic surveillance
slides.body:
**Calvin Schwabe** (UC Davis, 1927-2006) wrote *Veterinary Medicine and Human Health* (1st ed. 1964; 3rd ed. 1984) — the founding articulation of **'one medicine'**. Schwabe argued explicitly that human + animal + environmental health are inseparable. He trained on **hydatid disease (Echinococcus)** in Lebanon — a textbook dog↔sheep↔human zoonosis — + that experience grounded the framework in lived clinical reality.

**Modern One Health formulation**:
- **2004 Manhattan Principles** — Wildlife Conservation Society convened 12 principles ('Building Interdisciplinary Bridges to Health in a Globalized World') at a meeting led by **William Karesh** (WCS) + colleagues. The first formal modern statement of the integrated framework.
- **One Health Initiative** (Roger Mahr, Laura Kahn, Bruce Kaplan, Tom Monath, Lonnie King) — US-based advocacy + literature consolidation.
- **WHO + FAO + OIE Tripartite** (formalized 2010) → **Quadripartite** (with **UNEP** added 2022). The four-agency partnership now structures global AMR, zoonoses, food safety, + environmental health policy.
- **PREDICT / PREEMPT / DEEP VZN** (USAID-funded EID surveillance programs at wildlife-livestock-human interface; coordinated by EcoHealth Alliance under **Peter Daszak**, UC Davis One Health Institute, Smithsonian, WCS, + partners). PREDICT ran 2009-2020 + identified ~1200 novel viruses including several SARS-related coronaviruses in bats.
- **Global Virome Project** + **PREEMPT** (DARPA) + **CEPI** (Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, post-Ebola 2017) extend the architecture.

**Why veterinarians are central to pandemic prevention**:
- ~60% of known human infectious diseases + ~75% of EIDs are zoonotic (Jones, Daszak et al. 2008 *Nature*).
- Most spillovers reach a veterinarian (or wildlife biologist) before they reach human medicine — the **sentinel** role.
- Livestock + companion animals are amplifying intermediate hosts (camels for MERS; pigs for Nipah + influenza reassortment; mink + dairy cattle for SARS-CoV-2 + H5N1).
- Wildlife reservoirs require ecological + conservation framing (WCS, Karesh) + veterinary diagnostic capacity (laboratories + reference centers).
- Antimicrobial resistance is irreducibly a One Health problem — ~70% of medically-important antibiotic use (by weight) in US is in food animals; resistance flows between sectors.

**Modern surveillance architecture**:
- **WOAH WAHIS**: global animal-disease real-time reporting (~183 member countries).
- **WHO + GISRS**: human influenza surveillance.
- **FAO EMPRES**: livestock disease intelligence.
- **USDA APHIS + CDC + state health departments + state veterinarians**: US operational layer.
- **Wildlife health programs**: USFWS, USDA Wildlife Services, USGS National Wildlife Health Center, state wildlife agencies.
- **EcoHealth Alliance** + **WCS Health Program** + **Smithsonian Global Health** + **Karen Saylors / Labyrinth** + **CGIAR ILRI** + academic One Health institutes (Davis, Penn, Tufts, Minnesota, Cornell, Edinburgh-Roslin, RVC) form the research + capacity-building layer.

**Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) — the slow-motion One Health pandemic**:
- WHO ranks AMR among the top global health threats. ~1.27M deaths globally attributable to bacterial AMR in 2019 (Murray et al. *Lancet* 2022).
- Veterinary antibiotic use: medically-important antibiotics in US food animals declined ~36% from 2015 to 2022 (FDA Annual Summary), driven by **VFD (Veterinary Feed Directive 2017)** + restrictions on growth-promoter use + producer + consumer pressure.
- **WOAH list of antimicrobials of veterinary importance** + **WHO list of critically important antimicrobials for human medicine** structure global policy.
- WHO **GLASS** (Global Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System) + Quadripartite Joint Action Plan AMR 2024-29.
- Veterinary stewardship: AVMA + AAVPT + AABP + AAEP + AAFP guidelines on judicious use, formularies, prescription requirements, surveillance.

**Emerging-disease + climate + biodiversity nexus**:
- Habitat encroachment + wildlife trade + bushmeat consumption + intensive livestock + climate change accelerate spillover.
- **Drivers of spillover** (Plowright et al. 2017 framework): pathogen reservoir prevalence + human exposure + behavior + pathogen + host susceptibility.
- **Climate change** shifts vector ranges (Ixodes ticks northward; Aedes albopictus + aegypti expansion; Anopheles ranges) + alters wildlife + livestock disease patterns + facilitates new spillover events.
- **The 2024 H5N1 dairy outbreak + COVID-19 + Ebola + Nipah + Hendra + MERS + Zika** form the modern case set proving that One Health is not a slogan but the operational architecture of pandemic preparedness.

Veterinarians are full partners in this architecture — Schwabe's 1984 insight + Karesh's 2004 Manhattan Principles + Daszak's PREDICT surveillance + Quadripartite governance + Grandin-style measurable engineering of welfare are the present + future of the profession.

question.question: Trace a Nipah virus spillover event + apply the One Health response
question.goal: Reconstruct how a Nipah virus spillover would propagate from bat reservoir → human + design the One Health intervention.

steps.prompt: What is the natural reservoir of Nipah virus + which intermediate hosts have been implicated in different outbreaks?

acceptedAnswers: fruit bats (Pteropus); intermediate hosts: pigs (Malaysia 1998), date palm sap (Bangladesh — direct), horses (Hendra-related)

steps.reveal: **Pteropus fruit bats** are the natural reservoir of henipaviruses (Nipah, Hendra). **Malaysia 1998**: bats → pigs (consuming fruit dropped near pig farms) → human pig-farm workers; ~100 deaths + ~1M pigs culled. **Bangladesh + India 2001+ (recurrent)**: direct bat→human via date palm sap (bats licking collection pots); higher CFR ~70%; some human-to-human transmission (caregivers + healthcare workers). **Hendra virus** (related): bats → horses → veterinarians + handlers in Australia.

steps.prompt: Why is Nipah a One Health/Quadripartite test case?

acceptedAnswers: involves wildlife reservoir + livestock + food + human health + ecology — no single sector can manage it
requires wildlife (WCS/UNEP), livestock (WOAH/FAO), human (WHO), + environmental coordination

steps.reveal: Nipah requires **wildlife** (WCS + UNEP — bat ecology + conservation, habitat encroachment); **livestock** (WOAH + FAO — pig + horse + buffalo intermediate hosts, surveillance + biosecurity); **food** (FAO + national food safety — date palm sap collection practice, fruit handling); **human health** (WHO + national health systems — case detection, hospital infection control, contact tracing, PPE); **research** (vaccine development — CEPI funded mAb + vaccine candidates against Nipah). No single sector can resolve it — quintessential Quadripartite scenario.

steps.prompt: What surveillance architecture would detect Nipah early?

acceptedAnswers: bat serology + virology surveys (PREDICT-style), livestock syndromic surveillance, sentinel hospital network, lab capacity, community education + spillover-event reporting

steps.reveal: **Wildlife layer**: PREDICT-style virology + serology surveys of fruit-bat colonies (EcoHealth Alliance + ICDDR,B + Bangladesh + India partners); flying-fox ecology + habitat-encroachment monitoring; community-engaged sampling at human-bat interfaces. **Livestock layer**: WOAH/FAO syndromic surveillance for pig respiratory + neurologic disease, horse encephalitis (Australia for Hendra). **Human layer**: WHO + sentinel-hospital case-detection of viral encephalitis with travel/exposure history; rapid PCR + IgM. **Lab capacity**: BSL-4 reference labs (CDC, Geelong AAHL, ICDDR,B). **Community**: date-palm sap collection education (cover collection pots), bat-roost avoidance education, healthcare-worker PPE training. Linking the layers in real time is the One Health imperative.

steps.prompt: What is the modern medical countermeasure pipeline for Nipah?

acceptedAnswers: monoclonal antibodies (m102.4 anti-G), vaccine candidates (CEPI-funded mRNA + VSV-vectored + Hendra-G), ribavirin (historical, limited efficacy)

steps.reveal: **m102.4** (Christopher Broder + Australian/USU work) — human mAb against Nipah G protein; compassionate-use in some Hendra exposures; phase-1 trials. **CEPI-funded vaccine candidates**: Public Health Vaccines mRNA, Auro Vaccines + IAVI + others; **VSV-vectored** + **measles-vectored** + **Hendra G-glycoprotein** vaccines in preclinical/early clinical development. **Ribavirin**: historical, limited evidence. **Hendra equine vaccine** (Equivac HeV) is licensed in Australia + has dramatically reduced Hendra spillover to horses + thus to humans — a One Health vaccine that prevents reverse-zoonosis via the intermediate host. This is exactly the kind of integrated pipeline the Quadripartite + CEPI architecture is designed to fund + coordinate.

question.question: Why does the WHO/WOAH/FAO 'Zero by 30' rabies elimination strategy focus on mass canine vaccination rather than on treating human cases?
options: **Dog-mediated rabies kills ~59,000 people annually**, mostly in Asia + Africa; ~40% are children. Human PEP (post-exposure prophylaxis with HRIG + vaccine series) is 100% effective if started promptly, but it is **expensive (~USD 80-100+ per course in low-resource settings), often inaccessible (cold-chain, vaccine supply, transport, urgent presentation), + treats only those who survive the initial exposure window**. **Mass canine vaccination** (~70% coverage; the rabies-elimination threshold per Coleman + Dye + Lembo modeling) **interrupts transmission at the reservoir level** — cutting human exposure by orders of magnitude. Latin America has nearly eliminated human dog-mediated rabies through sustained mass canine vaccination (PAHO program 1980s+); the same strategy in Bali, Tanzania (Lembo + Cleaveland Serengeti program), parts of India is producing dramatic declines. **Zero by 30** (WHO + WOAH + FAO + GARC, 2018) is operationalized through: (1) annual mass dog vaccination, (2) responsible dog ownership, (3) human PEP access in endemic regions, (4) bite-case surveillance, (5) community engagement. The veterinary intervention is upstream + far more cost-effective than downstream human treatment — a textbook One Health argument anchored in Schwabe's framework + extended to global policy.
question.explanation: Mass canine vaccination at ~70% coverage interrupts rabies transmission at the reservoir level — orders of magnitude more cost-effective than human PEP downstream. WHO/WOAH/FAO 'Zero by 30' operationalizes this in endemic regions. Latin America has nearly eliminated human dog-mediated rabies via the strategy. A textbook Schwabe-style One Health argument.

hints: Upstream reservoir intervention vs downstream human treatment.
slides.workedSolution: Dog-mediated rabies kills ~59,000 humans/year, mostly Asia + Africa, ~40% children. Mass canine vaccination at ~70% coverage cuts transmission at the reservoir (Coleman, Dye, Lembo). Latin America's PAHO program nearly eliminated human cases. Zero by 30 (WHO/WOAH/FAO/GARC 2018) combines mass dog vaccination + responsible ownership + PEP access + surveillance. Veterinary intervention upstream is far more cost-effective than human PEP downstream — textbook One Health (Schwabe).

question.question: A dairy worker presents with conjunctivitis 3 d after exposure to HPAI-H5N1-positive cows on a Michigan dairy. Apply the One Health response.
question.scenario: Coordinate veterinary + public-health response to spillover.
question.modelAnswer: **Apply the One Health/Quadripartite architecture explicitly**. (1) **Human health pillar (CDC + state health department)**: case investigation + conjunctival + nasopharyngeal PCR for influenza A subtyping (CDC's BSL-3+ reference flu lab confirms H5N1 + B3.13 genotype); treatment with oseltamivir 75 mg PO BID × 5 d; baseline + convalescent serology; clinical follow-up for systemic symptoms. PPE counseling + return-to-work planning. (2) **Animal health pillar (USDA APHIS + state veterinarian + Michigan Department of Agriculture)**: trace farm — confirm HPAI in dairy herd via PCR on milk + nasal swabs; movement controls (Federal Order requires testing of lactating cows before interstate movement); biosecurity audit (milking-equipment hygiene — H5N1 spreads via milking units; PPE for milkers; visitor controls); decontamination protocols. (3) **Wildlife layer (USFWS + USGS National Wildlife Health Center + state wildlife agency)**: investigate wild-bird die-offs in flyway, mammal spillover (foxes, raccoons, sea lions, marine mammals), wild-bird surveillance. (4) **Food safety pillar (FDA + state food + agriculture)**: confirm pasteurization inactivates virus (it does — FDA bulk-tank sampling has shown viable virus in raw milk but inactivation after pasteurization); raw-milk distribution surveillance; consumer messaging. (5) **Worker protection (OSHA + NIOSH)**: PPE (eye protection, masks, gloves, coveralls) for dairy + poultry workers; antiviral prophylaxis for exposed workers; ill-worker reporting; multilingual outreach (many dairy workers Spanish-speaking; ensure linguistically + culturally competent communication). (6) **Reporting (WOAH WAHIS + WHO IHR)**: USDA reports to WOAH; CDC reports to WHO under IHR. (7) **Vaccine + therapeutic preparedness (BARDA + ASPR)**: stockpile of H5N1 candidate vaccine (CSL Seqirus, Sanofi, GSK); review readiness for scale-up if human-to-human transmission detected; develop bovine vaccines (Boehringer, Merck Animal Health, USDA). (8) **Research**: characterize PB2 mutations + receptor-binding preference + sequencing (NextStrain real-time phylogeny); academic + USDA + EcoHealth Alliance coordinated genomic surveillance. (9) **Risk communication**: AVMA + WSAVA + state vet associations issue guidance to practising vets, who are often the first to recognize unusual cow signs; engage media without panic. (10) **Long-term**: integrate findings into next pandemic-preparedness cycle. **This is exactly the architecture Schwabe + Karesh/WCS + Daszak/EcoHealth Alliance + the modern Quadripartite have constructed for precisely this scenario.** No single sector can manage spillover — the integrated response IS the One Health framework.
question.rubric: Identifies the Quadripartite (WOAH + WHO + FAO + UNEP) functions, coordinates animal + human + food + wildlife + worker protection + reporting + preparedness + communication, names specific institutional roles (USDA APHIS, CDC, FDA, USFWS, OSHA, BARDA), references the Schwabe + Karesh + Daszak/PREDICT/EcoHealth framework + recognizes integrated response as the architecture.

question.question: In a Bangladesh village, a Pteropus bat colony has 2000 individuals + an estimated Nipah seroprevalence of 5%. If date-palm sap collection contacts ~0.5% of bat-shedding events per season + sap-consumption among villagers is widespread, estimate exposed-villager order of magnitude (justify your estimate).
acceptedAnswers: 2000 × 0.05 = 100 seropositive bats; ~0.5% contact → ~0.5 contaminated events per season; multiple villagers per event → ~5-50 exposed; order ~10¹-10²
10s to 100s of exposures per season — depends on sap-consumption network
question.explanation: Rough order-of-magnitude estimate: 2000 bats × 0.05 seropositive = ~100 seropositive. If ~0.5% of bat-shedding events contact a sap-collection pot, ~0.5 contaminated events per season × variable shedding intensity = small absolute number of contaminated pots; each contaminated pot may be consumed by 10-50 villagers in shared-jar settings. Order of magnitude: **10¹-10²** exposures per season. **Observed Nipah outbreaks** in Bangladesh (ICDDR,B + Daszak + Luby) typically show clusters of 5-30 cases per season — consistent with the estimate. **Public-health intervention**: simple bamboo skirts ('bana' covers) prevent bat access to collection pots — cheap, locally-acceptable, evaluated by Khan + Luby + ICDDR,B + shown to interrupt the chain. Demonstrates that even rough quantitative reasoning identifies an actionable + feasible intervention. The One Health value chain — ecology → epidemiology → intervention — is concrete + measurable + cost-effective.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why veterinarians are central to pandemic preparedness + give two examples of spillover events where vet involvement was decisive.
question.rubric: Mentions: ~60% of human infectious diseases + ~75% of EIDs are zoonotic (Jones, Daszak et al. 2008); veterinarians are sentinels at the wildlife-livestock-human interface; the Schwabe 'one medicine' (1984) + Karesh/WCS Manhattan Principles (2004) + WOAH/WHO/FAO/UNEP Quadripartite (2022) architecture institutionalizes their role; PREDICT (USAID, EcoHealth Alliance under Daszak) + WAHIS surveillance illustrate. Examples: (1) Nipah Malaysia 1998 — pig veterinarians identified novel encephalitis in pigs before sustained human spread; massive pig cull contained the outbreak; (2) BSE/vCJD UK; (3) HPAI H5N1 2024 dairy cattle — USDA + state vets + dairy practitioners detected the unprecedented mammalian dairy outbreak + coordinated movement controls + biosecurity; (4) Hendra Australia — vets identified equine intermediate + designed vaccine. Concludes that veterinarians are operationally indispensable to One Health + pandemic preparedness.
